sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: What did the thirsty crow look for everywhere?
Choose the correct action word (verb) in the sentence: 'The children play in the park.'
Little drops of water and little grains of sand make the mighty:
Which word is a Proper Noun?
Choose the correct article: 'I eat ___ apple every morning.'
Which of these is our National Bird?
Choose the correct pronoun to replace the naming word: 'Sita is my friend. ___ is a good girl.'
Who treats us when we fall sick in our town?
What tells you that a rose is nearby without looking at it?
Which of the following is a describing word (adjective)?
How did the clever monkey fool the crocodile? (Answer in 1-2 sentences)
questions.answer: The clever monkey told the crocodile that he left his heart on the tree. When the crocodile swam back, the monkey jumped to safety.

questions.question_text: Name any two important places you see between your home and your school.
questions.answer: I see a big park and a hospital between my home and my school.

questions.question_text: Why do we write letters to our family members who live far away?
questions.answer: We write letters to tell them how we are doing and to show them that we love and miss them.

questions.question_text: What are two things you find 'fun' to do on a Sunday? Use action words.
questions.answer: It is fun to paint pictures and ride my bicycle on a Sunday.

questions.question_text: How did the thirsty crow solve his problem and drink the water?
questions.answer: The crow dropped small stones into the pot until the water came up to the top, and then he drank it.

sections.section_name: Section C - Grammar & Matching (Fill in the Blanks)

questions.question_text: Fill in the blanks with the correct Prepositions (in, on, under, behind): 1. The books are kept ___ the bag. 2. The cat is sleeping ___ the bed. 3. The vase is placed ___ the table. 4. The sun is hiding ___ the clouds.
Join the following sentences using the joining words (Conjunctions) 'and' or 'but': 1. I like apples. I like bananas. 2. He ran very fast. He missed the school bus.
questions.answer: 1. I like apples and bananas. 2. He ran very fast but he missed the school bus.

questions.question_text: Imagine you have a magical bicycle. Write 3-4 sentences describing what it looks like and where you would ride it.
questions.answer: My magical bicycle is bright blue with shiny silver wheels. It has soft wings that can flap and fly in the air. I would ride my bicycle all the way up to the clouds and say hello to the birds.

questions.question_text: Look up at the sky in your imagination. Describe two fun shapes you see in the clouds. What do they look like they are doing?
questions.answer: I see a big, fluffy white cloud that looks like a sleeping giant dog. Next to it, there is another cloud shaped like a dancing rabbit that is hopping across the sky.
